About the role

Scale's Global Public Sector team uses AI to address critical challenges facing the public sector around the world. As an Applied AI Engineer, you'll build AI that runs inside production systems used by national health and government organisations.

You'll own scoped components of those systems, such as a model integration, agent tool, API, data pipeline, or evaluation, from implementation through to delivery. Senior engineers set the system-level design and client commitments, so you can go deep on making your components work reliably on real data.

What you'll do

- Own the implementation, testing, and delivery of defined AI components within an established system design

- Build agent tools, model integrations, and the backend services and APIs they depend on

- Run and extend evaluations within an established framework, interpret results, investigate common failure modes, and flag regressions

- Debug production issues in the components you own and resolve them using the team's engineering practices

- Communicate progress and blockers early, and take responsibility for delivery dates within your scope

- Work directly with client teams on the requirements and feedback for your components

- Share what you learn with the team as you build public sector domain expertise

What we look for

- Experience building and shipping production software, with proficiency in Python and working knowledge of at least one of TypeScript, Java, or C++

- Hands-on experience integrating models or AI/ML components into a production application, such as calling LLMs, building retrieval or agent tooling, or deploying a trained model

- A working understanding of ML evaluation: how to read results, spot regressions, and identify common causes of model failure

- Experience owning a defined piece of work through testing, release, and production debugging

- Strong problem-solving skills and a data-driven approach to iterating on models and datasets

- Clear written and verbal communication, including raising blockers and trade-offs early

Nice to have

- Experience with cloud ML platforms such as AWS, GCP, or Azure

- Exposure to agentic workflows, retrieval-augmented generation, or context engineering

- Experience handling regulated or sensitive data

Where this role sits

Your primary accountability covers production AI behaviour, its backend integration, and the evaluation required for a specific customer. Our Radio Products Team is seeking a hybrid
**Software Engineer, Embedded Linux - Unmanned Aircraft Systems.**
You would be responsible for working on next generation self-networking UAS/Drone based embedded radios for domestic and foreign defense forces. A typical day might start with you working in your personal office designing and implementing embedded Linux user-space applications, third party APIs or defining product customization details. It could move into one of our many state-of-the-art labs with your teammates to bring up your design on physical radio hardware or UAS platform.  Enhancing cohesiveness and maintaining team morale is a responsibility of all our team members, as is the ambition for self-improvement and talent development. Through this dedication to unity and professional advancement, each team member is directly impacting the successful outcome of TrellisWare’s deliverables and setting the tone for our core values of delivering excellence, pushing boundaries, and empowering people.

The
**essential duties and responsibilities**
include:

* Design, implement, and integrate radio software for an embedded Linux target for UAS embedded solutions (headless applications, servers, and drivers)
* Perform feasibility studies, and performance analysis of software defined radio embedded Linux components within a UAS platform
* Interface with common Linux services and protocols
* Configure or adapt Linux board support packages
* Document and present design alternatives using standard professional practices and corporate defined engineering processes
* Develop relationships with team members built on trust and respect.

**Education and work experience**
requirements are:

* Bachelor's degree in Electrical/Computer Engineering, Computer Science or related field of study required.
* Minimum of four years’ experience integrating with embedded Linux and four years of embedded software development experience
* General proficiency of C++ and Python
* Two years of experience with Yocto Project or other complex build systems
* Experience with command and control (C2) links, flight controller integration, and software defined radios
* Experience with common lab test equipment (i.e. oscilloscope, logic analyzer)
* Experience with Object-oriented design, data link layer and device drivers as well as ARM based processors

To be considered for this position, you would need to meet, at a minimum, the

* Experience with network protocols: HTTP/HTTPS, TCP/UDP, SSL/TLS
* Experience integrating with optimized video encoding protocols
* Working knowledge of network switches, bridges, and routers
* Distributed revision control systems and common embedded Linux development tools (i.e. compilers, linkers, and debuggers)
